lines: That's how many Tullia climbed every morning, with a jar of water on her shoulder.
It was heavy. The fountain was three streets away.
But the old widow on the top floor could no longer walk.
Julia never thanked her. Not once. She only ever said one thing.
The landlord found Tullia on the stairs, and handed her a small cloth bundle.
Inside were coins. Years of them. Every coin Julia had saved.
And a broken piece of pottery, with a few words scratched into it.

shots.card:
“You were always late.
So I always knew you’d come.”

lines.say: You were always late... so I always knew you'd come.

lines: Some people never learn how to say thank you.
So they say it the only way they can... by waiting for you.
